article_title: ICE detains Canadian mom with 7-year-old autistic daughter
article_content:
A Canadian woman and her 7-year-old autistic daughter are being held at a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center in Texas, with her American husband left fighting to free them.
Tania Warner and her daughter Ayla, both born in British Columbia, were with her husband Edward Warner, an American citizen, driving in Sarita, Texas, when they reached an immigration checkpoint just over a week ago.
After fingerprinting both Tania and Ayla, agents detained them and said the husband was free to go. Edward told CTV that his wife moved to the U.S. five years ago and that she had a work permit.
Newsweek reached out to DHS for comment on the Warners’ cases, with a spokesperson not initially answering specific questions on their status.
"If you overstay your visa and are in the country illegally, you will be arrested," the spokesperson said. "To be clear: Work authorization does NOT give someone legal status to be in our country."
Tania Warner and her daughter are now being held at the Dilley Detention Center, which has been a major cause for concern for Democratic lawmakers in recent months with reportedly poor conditions.
Why It Matters
Under President Donald Trump, there have been increased reports of immigrants who either have, or believe they have, legal status being detained by federal agents. The White House argues it is enforcing immigration rules previous administrations failed to, but critics have countered that by highlighting the president’s promise to go after the "worst of the worst," not those in the country seeking to follow the rules and not committing any crimes.
What To Know
Edward Warner told Canadian media that the family was stopped by federal agents on March 14 at a permanent checkpoint they had driven through before without incident. He and Tania presented their identification, with agents then taking his wife into an office for fingerprinting.
ICE agents then took his stepdaughter in to get her prints, Edward said, and neither returned. The pair were initially transported to a Rio Grande detention facility, before being transferred to Dilley.
In a statement to Global News, Tania said that her daughter was struggling with the conditions at Dilley, including stress and overstimulation.
The outlet reported that Tania applied for legal status four years ago, but her application was denied because Edward Warner is a registered sex offender in Texas because of an incident in his teenage years. The couple then found a way for her to apply without his name attached to her application.
CTV reported that Tania had a work permit that declared her a "legal alien." DHS has not given details confirming this at time of publishing.
What People Are Saying
Edward Warner, speaking to Global News: "They were sleeping on the floor using the floor masks to keep warm because all they had were those like tin space blanket things, and they said the food was terrible, the guards were awful, just the whole experience is gonna be very traumatic for the both of them."
Democratic Texas Representative Vicente Gonzalez, on X, on March 20: "My office is in contact with the Warner family and pressing for their immediate release. Tania has a work permit and is part of the fabric of our Kingsville community; she nor her daughter Ayla, a 7-year-old with autism, should be in detention. We must bring them home and reunite yet another family being ripped apart by this Administration’s rogue immigration enforcement operations."
A DHS spokesperson told Newsweek: "The Dilley Facility provides a comprehensive medical screening within 12 hours of arrival for each detainee, including by a pediatrician for infants and children. Pediatric screenings include growth, developmental, behavioral, and nutritional assessments, and all evaluations cover acute conditions, mental health, suicide risk, medications, allergies, and special needs. During initial screenings, the facility’s medical personnel review medications families bring with them for continuity and provide urgent and life-sustaining medications immediately.
"Being in detention is a choice. We encourage all parents to take control of their departure with the CBP Home App. The United States is offering illegal aliens $2,600 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return."
What Happens Next
Edward Warner was said to be raising funds for an attorney and has vowed to keep fighting to keep his family together in the U.S.
